newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Fran could be as strong as Hugo - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Fran could be as strong as Hugo - WSC.

text.p: Hurricane Fran, which is about as large as Hurricane Hugo and has the potential to become as strong, is forecast to make landfall in the Carolinas by late Thursday or early Friday with top winds near 125 mph, Weather Services Corp said.
Heavy rains of 5-10 inches are expected along its path and tides 12-16 feet above normal are possible near and northeast of where the centre makes landfall.
Fran, with 115 mph winds, is currently 335 miles southeast of Charleston, South Carolina, moving northwest at 12 mph.

Hurricane warnings are in effect from north of Brunswick, Georgia to the North Carolina/Virginia Border, including Pamlico and Albemarle Sounds. Preparations in this area should be rushed to completion.

A Hurricane Watch is in efffect from north of the North Carolina/Virginia Border to Chincoteague, Virgina, including the Greaters Hampton Roads Area. A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect from Flagler Beach, Florida to Brunswick, Georgia.

A Tropical Storm Warning also remains in effect for the extreme northwestern Bahamas for the islands of Abaco and Grand Bahama. Rain squalls, strong winds, and 3-6 foot seas are likely in the northwestern Bahamas, WSC added.
